themes_detail.label: Air Quality Crisis in Belmont
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints spiked to 4 this week—a 1500% jump from the 0.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.66)—signaling an acute environmental event affecting CD206 residents THIS WEEK that requires immediate investigation.
evidence: 4 air quality complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 8.66 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Timing: acute event within last 7 days, not chronic pattern
reporting_angles: What triggered the air quality spike this week? (industrial emission, construction, weather event, traffic surge?)
Which neighborhoods within Belmont/East Tremont are most affected? Map the complaints.
Is this related to any active development permits (136 new buildings filed in last 90 days) or construction activity?

themes_detail.label: Homelessness & Encampment Surge
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 8 THIS WEEK—a 433% spike from the 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 5.81)—paired with vendor enforcement complaints at 9 this week (350% above baseline), suggesting a visible street-level crisis emerging in real-time.
evidence: 8 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average (433% increase)
9 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly average (350% increase)
Combined signal suggests deteriorating street conditions and informal economies in real-time
reporting_angles: Where are encampments forming? Which blocks or parks are becoming focal points?
What services (outreach, shelter capacity, sanitation) exist in Belmont, and are they adequate?
Interview residents and business owners about visible changes in the past week.
Connect to repeated CB budget requests for parks, senior centers, and social services—are these unmet needs fueling street-level crisis?

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise & Illegal Parking Spike
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints more than doubled to 12 THIS WEEK from a 4.6 weekly average (160% increase), while illegal parking remains elevated at 136 complaints 2 weeks ago (85% above baseline)—together painting a picture of deteriorating traffic enforcement and street quality.
evidence: 12 vehicle noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.6 weekly average (160% spike, z-score: 2.65)
136 illegal parking complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 73.5 weekly average (85% spike, z-score: 4.3)
Two-week sustained pattern indicates ongoing traffic management breakdown
reporting_angles: Are specific corridors (e.g., Grand Concourse, Southern Boulevard) seeing illegal drag racing or modified vehicles?
What NYPD enforcement presence exists on the streets? Are parking and traffic enforcement proportionate to complaints?
Interview residents about sleep disruption and safety concerns from vehicle noise.

themes_detail.label: Police Call-Out Spike (3 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matter complaints spiked to 10 three weeks ago—a 515% increase from 1.6 weekly average (z-score: 8.44)—indicating a significant public safety concern that may still be unresolved.
evidence: 10 non-emergency police complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.6 weekly average (515% increase, z-score: 8.44)
Signal is 3 weeks old, not current, but indicates prior acute event
reporting_angles: What triggered the police call-out spike 3 weeks ago? (assault, theft, disturbance?)
Has the underlying issue been resolved, or are residents still reporting related concerns?
Pull NYPD crime data for Belmont/East Tremont over the past month to contextualize the 311 spike.

themes_detail.label: Heat/Hot Water Complaints Plummet
themes_detail.summary: Heat/hot water complaints dropped 79% to 35 THIS WEEK from a 163.8 weekly average (z-score: -2.98)—a significant seasonal decline suggesting either genuine weather warming, successful repairs, or potential under-reporting that deserves verification given this category dominates 311 volume.
evidence: 35 heat/hot water complaints THIS WEEK vs. 163.8 weekly average (79% decline)
Heat/hot water is the #1 complaint category by volume (2,147 complaints over 90 days)
Timing suggests seasonal shift, but magnitude is unusual
reporting_angles: Is this a seasonal effect (warmer weather) or evidence of successful landlord compliance/city enforcement?
Spot-check buildings in Belmont/East Tremont: are landlords maintaining heat/hot water adequately, or are residents under-reporting due to resignation?
Compare to prior-year data: is this decline consistent with historical weather patterns?
